rows.transcript_1:
Here is an activity to relax your body: 

Sit comfortably and close your eyes if you can. 
Imagine a golden ring scanning your body from your feet to your head.  
Pay attention as it moves up and down your body. Are there any areas that feel tense? Numb? Painful?  
Focus on those areas for a moment. Breathe into the area and, when you breathe out, try to let go of any tension or pain.  
Do this for a few breaths.  

Open your eyes. How does your body feel now?

You can also try this next time you find yourself lying in bed unable to sleep!
rows.transcript_2:
Cubalah untuk ambil masa untuk merehatkan tubuh badan anda setiap hari.

Berikut ialah satu aktiviti untuk merehatkan tubuh badan anda:

Duduk dengan selesa dan pejamkan mata jika boleh.
Bayangkan sebuah alat pengimbas keemasan mengimbas tubuh anda dari kaki hingga ke kepala.
Perhatikan pergerakannya naik dan turun pada tubuh badan anda. Adakah ada bahagian yang terasa tegang? Kebas? Atau sakit?
Fokus pada bahagian itu seketika. Tarik nafas dan hembus nafas perlahan sambil menggerakkan sedikit tubuh badan anda yang berasa tegang, kebas atau sakit secara perlahan-lahan. 
Ulang dan tarik nafas beberapa kali.

Satu.....Dua.....Tiga....

Buka mata anda perlahan-lahan. Bagaimana tubuh anda rasa sekarang?

Anda juga boleh cuba latihan ini apabila anda sedang berbaring di atas katil dan mengalami kesukaran untuk tidur!

text_1_facilitator.eng:
To keep your child safe, talk with them about which places are safe to go and which are not, and teach them how to be careful when they meet people they don't know.

4️⃣Here are four steps to help you keep your child safe in your community:

rows.text_1_facilitator:
To keep your child safe, talk with them about which places are safe to go and which are not, and teach them how to be careful when they meet people they don't know.

4️⃣Here are four steps to help you keep your child safe in your community:

section_1_text.eng:
📝 Draw a map of your community.
🚩 Include the main places in your community: your house, streets in your neighbourhood, pre-school, daycare, and other places. 
👋Draw and identify pictures of trusted people who your child can go to when they feel unsafe. These can be you and your spouse, other family members, or teachers.

section_2_text.eng:
🔑 Talk about the safe and unsafe places on your map. For example, let your child know that the street is not a safe place, even if their toy or ball goes there. 
🔵 CIRCLE the places that are safe for children.
❌ CROSS OFF any places that are unsafe for your child. For example, areas under construction, parking areas, or unfamiliar buildings.

section_3_text.eng:
❗ Discuss with your child why it is important to ALWAYS have an adult with them when they go outside. 
🧸Make sure your child knows it’s okay to walk or run inside if a stranger tries to talk to them or asks them to go somewhere. 
👀 Discuss with your child safe places they can run if a stranger approaches them – such as your home, or a neighbour’s home. 
🚩 Mark these areas clearly on your map.

section_4_text.eng:
🔔Practise! Practise! Practise! 
👑 Using toys or puppets, role-play scenarios where a stranger approaches. Ask your child what the toy should do. Children find it less scary to pretend that someone else is in danger. 
⭐ Praise when your child chooses the correct response, such as running away, shouting for help, or finding a trusted adult.
